signature: SUBROUTINE DGGEV( JOBVL, JOBVR, N, A, LDA, B, LDB, ALPHAR, ALPHAI,

params.name: jobvl
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
-   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.

params.name: jobvr
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
-   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten.
params.workDependent: the generalized Schur form S is unique only up to signs, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten.
params.workDependent: the triangular T is unique only up to signs, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change

params.name: BETA
params.reference:
On exit, (`ALPHAR(j)` + `ALPHAI(j)`\*i)/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues. If `ALPHAI(j)` is zero, then the j-th eigenvalue is real; if positive, then the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, with `ALPHAI(j+1)` negative.

Note: the quotients `ALPHAR(j)`/`BETA(j)` and `ALPHAI(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio $\alpha$/$\beta$. However, `ALPHAR` and `ALPHAI` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).

params.name: VL
params.reference: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
params.workDependent: each left eigenvector is unique only up to a scalar factor of unit size, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change

params.name: ldvl
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix `VL`. $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge 1$, and if `JOBVL = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge N$.

params.name: VR
params.reference: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
params.workDependent: each right eigenvector is unique only up to a scalar factor of unit size, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change

params.name: ldvr
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix `VR`. $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge 1$, and if `JOBVR = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge N$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,8 \, N)$. For good performance, `LWORK` must generally be larger.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `= 1,...,N`:  The QZ iteration failed.  No eigenvectors have been calculated, but `ALPHAR(j)`, `ALPHAI(j)`, and `BETA(j)` should be correct for $j=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N.
-   `> N`: =N+1: other than QZ iteration failed in DHGEQZ. =N+2: error return from DTGEVC.

overrides.reason: DGGEV hands its LWORK to DGEQRF, DORMQR and DORGQR, which pick their block size from LWORK and fall back to unblocked code when it is short of the optimum. The blocked and unblocked QR steps round differently, and the QZ iteration that follows can then reach a generalized Schur form (S,T) whose rows and columns differ by signs, with eigenvectors scaled by -1 (real) or by a different complex unit (complex pairs). ALPHAR, ALPHAI and BETA do not depend on LWORK beyond rounding; the module's tests check the eigenvalues at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (ticket 0100).

set.params.A.workDependent: the generalized Schur form S is unique only up to signs, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change
set.params.B.workDependent: the triangular T is unique only up to signs, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change
set.params.VL.workDependent: each left eigenvector is unique only up to a scalar factor of unit size, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change
set.params.VR.workDependent: each right eigenvector is unique only up to a scalar factor of unit size, which the LWORK-dependent QR blocking can change
